newsitem.title: INDIA: India Smithkline Beecham offers bonus.
newsitem.headline: India Smithkline Beecham offers bonus.

text.p: India's Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd on Tuesday proposed a bonus offer of three shares for every five shares held, a company statement said.
"This will capitalise 170 million rupees and still leave a robust surplus in company reserves. The last bonus in the ratio of 1:1 was issued in 1995," the statement said.

The company's after-tax profit jumped 30 percent to 469.4 million rupees for the financial year ended on December 31. Profit before tax was 793.1 million rupees, it said without giving a comparative figure for 1995.
Sales soared to 4.97 billion rupees in 1996. It did not provide a comparative figure.

"The profits have allowed us the freedom to reward our shareholders and also to build on our position of strength through an increased allocation of 299.3 million rupees towards the general reserves and surplus account," the statement quoted managing director Simon Scarff as saying.
The company had also announced during 1996 two interim dividends totalling 60 percent, the statement said.
The healthy financial performance was attributable to the company's two brands in malted food industry, "Horlicks" and "Boost", it added.
Exports rose 45.4 percent in 1996 compared to the previous year as the company's products made significant inroads in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and the Middle East.

"Building on the brand equity of Boost and Horlicks, the company plans to enter into new product categories which will continue to deliver a very sound and healthy double-digit growth," the statement said.
Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd (SBCH) is an Indian associate of Britain's Smithkline Beecham Plc.
